meaning: The valley where the game is set; preserve it as the proper name of the region and as part of titles such as Stardew Valley Fair.
The main town in Stardew Valley and the home of most villagers, shops, and community events.
A farm is land used for crops, animals, and buildings; capitalized The Farm means the player's home location.
Farmer is the player character or a person who runs a farm; farmhand specifically means a non-host player in multiplayer.
A named resident whom the player can speak to, befriend, and often give gifts to.
Pelican Town's abandoned civic building, restored by completing bundles for the Junimos.
A themed set of requested items delivered to the Community Center to unlock a reward or town repair.
Joja is the corporate brand and organization; JojaMart is its local supermarket and the center of the alternative town-development route.
Small forest spirits who collect bundle offerings, restore the Community Center, and can later help harvest crops.
A deity worshipped in the setting; the name appears in blessings, religious symbols, and the Altar of Yoba.
A rare star-shaped fruit that permanently increases the player's maximum energy.
A rare purple metal used for top-tier tools, equipment, buildings, and crafting; it also names the highest ordinary item-quality tier.
A tropical island in the Fern Islands that opens as a major late-game area with its own farm, volcano, quests, and currency.
A desert region reached by bus after the Community Center vault or its Joja equivalent is completed.
The multi-floor mining dungeon in the Mountain; mine level means the numbered floor currently reached.
A difficult, effectively bottomless mining dungeon in Calico Desert, separate from the Mines.
One of the game's four 28-day periods, which controls crops, forage, fish, weather, schedules, and festivals.
The first season of each year and the season in which a new game begins.
The second season of each year, following Spring.
The third season of each year; the game consistently uses the American English word Fall rather than Autumn.
The fourth season of each year, when most ordinary outdoor crops do not grow.
A single playable date; many tasks, schedules, machines, and limits reset or advance overnight.
A full cycle of Spring, Summer, Fall, and Winter; years are numbered and have no fixed upper limit.
A scheduled seasonal event with unique dialogue, activities, shops, competitions, or rewards.
The resource consumed by many tool actions; food and sleep restore it, while Stardrops raise its maximum.
The player's hit points in dangerous areas; reaching zero causes the player to pass out and lose money or items.
A hidden modifier that affects many random outcomes; daily luck changes each day and is reported by the Fortune Teller.
A player ability improved through related actions; skill level is the current rank, normally from 0 to 10.
The skill raised mainly by harvesting crops and caring for farm animals.
The skill raised by breaking rocks and mining nodes, associated chiefly with the Pickaxe.
The skill raised by gathering wild items and chopping trees, associated chiefly with the Axe.
The skill raised by catching fish and collecting from Crab Pots, associated with rods, bait, and tackle.
The skill raised by defeating monsters and associated with weapons, defense, and critical hits.
Points earned through skill-related actions; enough experience raises a skill level and later contributes to Mastery.
A permanent skill specialization chosen at levels 5 and 10 that grants a specific gameplay bonus.
A late-game progression system unlocked after reaching level 10 in all five skills, with one mastery reward track per skill.
The late-game completion measure tracked in Qi's Walnut Room; reaching 100% unlocks the Summit ending sequence.
The relationship score with a villager; points are displayed as hearts and unlock dialogue, recipes, mail, and events.
An item given to a villager; its gift taste is Loved, Liked, Neutral, Disliked, or Hated and determines the friendship change.
Marriage is the relationship state after a successful proposal and wedding; spouse is the player's married partner.
A tracked task with objectives and rewards; Help Wanted requests are short timed quests posted outside Pierre's store.
A larger timed request accepted from the Special Orders board, usually with unique dialogue and rewards.
The player-menu tab and item storage carried by the player, limited by the current backpack capacity.
The main in-game menu containing Inventory, Skills, Social, Map, Crafting, Collections, and Options tabs.
The interface that lists active quests and their current objectives.
The player-menu tab that records shipped items, fish, artifacts, minerals, cooking, achievements, and letters.
Creating an item instantly from ingredients through the Crafting tab or a Workbench.
Preparing food from ingredients in a kitchen or Cookout Kit using learned cooking recipes.
A learned formula that specifies ingredients for a craftable item or cooked dish; keep crafting and cooking recipes distinct in context.
The permanent farm layout selected during character creation, such as Standard Farm or Meadowlands Farm.
A cultivated plant grown from seed and harvested for produce; most crops are restricted by season.
Planting materials: seeds grow ordinary crops, starters grow trellis or specialty crops, and saplings grow fruit trees.
To collect a mature crop or other farm product; as a noun, the produce collected.
A wild item gathered from the ground rather than grown as a normal crop.
An item produced by a farm animal, such as milk, an egg, wool, or truffle.
A processed product made in a machine, such as wine, cheese, jelly, or mayonnaise.
An item's grade, shown by no star or a Silver, Gold, or Iridium star and often affecting value or effectiveness.
Reusable equipment for farm and exploration actions, including the Axe, Hoe, Pickaxe, Watering Can, Scythe, Rod, and Pan.
The tool used to till soil and uncover artifact spots and other buried items.
The refillable tool used to water crops; upgrades increase the charged watering area and capacity.
The tool used to chop trees, stumps, logs, and branches.
The tool used to break stones, ore nodes, and placed flooring or equipment.
The tool used to cut grass, weeds, and certain crops; it does not consume energy.
The tool used to catch fish; both Rod and Pole occur in official item names and interface text.
An attachment for a fishing rod or Crab Pot that changes bite rate, catch behavior, or catches.
A reusable fishing-rod attachment with a special effect; many individual tackle items are named as bobbers.
Ore is a raw mined resource; a bar is refined metal produced by smelting ore in a Furnace.
A breakable mineral container processed by a blacksmith; an Omni Geode can contain minerals from every ordinary geode pool.
A soil treatment applied to tilled soil or trees to affect crop quality, growth speed, water retention, or tree growth.
A placed machine that automatically waters a fixed pattern of nearby tilled tiles every morning.
The country that contains Stardew Valley, Pelican Town, Calico Desert, and the Fern Islands.
A foreign state at war with the Ferngill Republic during the game; Kent was held there as a prisoner of war.
The sea along the southern coast of Stardew Valley that contains the Fern Islands.
An archipelago in the Gem Sea that includes Ginger Island and belongs to the Ferngill Republic.
A large city outside Stardew Valley, frequently mentioned by villagers as the region's urban center.
Dwarves are an ancient underground people; Dwarvish names their language, artifacts, technology, and forge.
A subterranean people that includes Krobus and once fought the Dwarves in the Elemental Wars.
The historical conflict between the Dwarves and the Shadow People referenced in lore and dialogue.
The magic user living in the Wizard's Tower; Wizard is his usual label and M. Rasmodius is his name.
A friendly member of the Shadow People who lives in the Sewers and can become the player's roommate.
The same mysterious challenge-giver is displayed as Mister Qi in the canonical NPC name table and as Mr. Qi throughout most dialogue and interface text.
The player's grandfather, who leaves the farm to the player and later returns in spirit to evaluate their progress.
Pelican Town's mayor, commonly addressed by his title and responsible for many town notices, festivals, and services.
The large forest region southwest of the farm, containing Marnie's Ranch, the Wizard's Tower, and entrances to several other areas.
The northern outdoor region containing the Carpenter's Shop, the Mines, the Adventurer's Guild, and the lake.
The coastal area south of Pelican Town, containing the Fish Shop, tidal pools, and several festivals.
The transit area east of the farm; after repair, its bus carries the player to Calico Desert.
The northern rail area opened after the earthquake, containing the train platform, Spa, and Witch's Swamp entrance.
A mineral-producing area east of the Mountain, unlocked by repairing the bridge.
A hidden forest area northwest of Cindersap Forest, blocked by a large log until the Axe is upgraded.
An underground location unlocked with the Rusty Key and inhabited by Krobus.
The bathhouse by the Railroad where standing in the pool restores Energy and Health.
A ten-floor dungeon inside the Ginger Island volcano, ending at the Forge.
Mr. Qi's late-game room on Ginger Island, where the player accepts Qi's Special Orders and tracks Perfection.
The organization and building beside the Mines that sells combat gear and tracks Monster Eradication Goals.
Pierre's shop in Pelican Town, the main local source of crop seeds and backpack upgrades.
Gus's tavern in Pelican Town, commonly shortened to the saloon in dialogue.
Robin's business in the Mountain, used to buy supplies, construct farm buildings, and upgrade or renovate homes.
Clint's shop and profession; the shop upgrades tools, processes geodes, and sells ore and coal.
Marnie's home and shop in Cindersap Forest, where the player buys animals and animal supplies.
Willy's shop on the Beach, where the player buys fishing rods and supplies and gains access to his boat.
Gunther's Pelican Town institution, where the player donates artifacts and minerals and reads recovered Lost Books.
Sandy's shop in Calico Desert and the entrance building for the Casino.
Mr. Qi's club behind the Oasis, where Casino games and prizes use Qi Coins.
A late-game entertainment venue where the player can invite a guest to watch a movie and buy concessions.
The two level-5 Farming professions: Rancher improves animal-product prices, while Tiller improves crop prices.
The level-10 Rancher professions: Coopmaster specializes in coop animals, while Shepherd specializes in barn animals and sheep.
The level-10 Tiller professions: Artisan increases Artisan Good prices, while Agriculturist makes crops grow faster.
The two level-5 Fishing professions: Fisher improves fish prices, while Trapper reduces Crab Pot crafting costs.
The level-10 Fisher professions: Angler further improves fish prices, while Pirate increases treasure-finding chance.
The level-10 Trapper professions: Mariner prevents trash in Crab Pots, while Luremaster removes their bait requirement.
The two level-5 Foraging professions: Forester increases wood yield, while Gatherer can double harvested forage.
The level-10 Forester professions: Lumberjack enables Hardwood drops from all trees, while Tapper improves syrup prices.
The level-10 Gatherer professions: Botanist makes foraged items highest quality, while Tracker reveals nearby forage locations.
The two level-5 Mining professions: Miner adds ore per vein, while Geologist can make gems appear in pairs.
The level-10 Miner professions: Blacksmith improves metal-bar prices, while Prospector increases coal-finding chance.
The level-10 Geologist professions: Excavator increases geode finds, while Gemologist improves gem and mineral prices.
The two level-5 Combat professions: Fighter raises damage and Health, while Scout improves critical-hit chance.
The level-10 Fighter professions: Brute further raises damage, while Defender raises maximum Health.
The level-10 Scout professions: Acrobat reduces special-move cooldown, while Desperado greatly increases critical-hit damage.
The player's home on the farm, upgraded by Robin to add rooms and features such as a kitchen, nursery, and cellar.
A farm building where crops and fruit trees can grow regardless of season.
A farm building for chickens and other small animals; it can be upgraded to Big Coop and Deluxe Coop.
A farm building for cows and other large animals; it can be upgraded to Big Barn and Deluxe Barn.
A farm building that stores hay cut from grass for feeding animals.
A farm building that comes with a horse the player can ride for faster travel.
A customizable farm building used as indoor space for machines, storage, furniture, or crops in pots.
A small farm home assigned to a farmhand in multiplayer and upgradeable like the Farmhouse.
A farm building where a fish population grows, requests items, and produces roe or other goods.
A farm building for raising Slimes and collecting Slime Balls.
A magical farm building whose Junimos harvest mature crops within a fixed area.
A farm container used to sell items overnight; its contents are summarized on the end-of-day shipping screen.
A Scarecrow protects nearby crops from crows; a Rarecrow is a collectible design with the same basic purpose.
A processing machine that turns fruit into wine, vegetables into juice, and certain crops into beverages.
A processing machine that makes jelly, pickles, aged roe, and caviar.
A cellar machine used to age wine, beer, pale ale, mead, cheese, and goat cheese to higher quality.
A processing machine that smelts ore with coal into metal bars and refines certain other materials.
A processing machine that converts wood into coal.
A processing machine that turns eggs and certain related products into mayonnaise.
A processing machine that turns milk into cheese and goat milk into goat cheese.
A processing machine that turns wool into cloth.
A processing machine that makes truffle oil and can also process corn, sunflower seeds, and sunflowers into oil.
A processing machine that converts most fishing trash into useful resources.
A processing machine that usually converts a crop into seeds of the same crop.
A processing machine that combines a fish with coal to make Smoked Fish while preserving the fish's quality.
A processing machine that turns batches of fruit or edible mushrooms into dried goods and grapes into raisins.
A placed fishing trap that normally requires bait and catches shellfish, snails, or trash overnight.
A processing machine that produces honey outdoors outside Winter, with nearby flowers changing the honey type.
A processing device attached to a mature tree to collect syrup, resin, tar, or other tree products over time.
A one-use item that instantly teleports the player to the location named after the colon, such as Farm or Beach.
The Spring 13 festival in Pelican Town, centered on an egg hunt.
The Spring 24 festival in Cindersap Forest, where the player may ask an eligible villager to dance.
The Summer 11 festival on the Beach, centered on adding an ingredient to the communal soup.
The Summer 28 evening festival on the Beach, where villagers watch migrating moonlight jellies.
The Fall 16 festival in Pelican Town, featuring games, Star Tokens, and the Grange Display competition.
The Fall 27 night festival in Pelican Town, featuring a haunted maze.
The Winter 8 festival in Cindersap Forest, centered on ice sculptures and a fishing contest.
A three-night Winter 15–17 festival on the Beach with special merchants, entertainment, and submarine fishing.
The Winter 25 festival in Pelican Town, featuring a secret gift exchange.
A three-day Spring 15–17 event in Calico Desert with rotating villagers, challenges, shops, and Calico Eggs.
A two-day Winter 12–13 fishing event on the Beach with squid-catch prize tiers.
A two-day Summer 20–21 fishing event in Cindersap Forest based on catching Rainbow Trout and collecting tags.

The title-screen command that opens the list of existing saved games.
The title-screen and gameplay label for cooperative multiplayer, including hosting and joining farms.
The menu section for controls, sound, graphics, interface, multiplayer, and other game settings.
Writing the current game state to a save file, normally performed when the player ends the day by sleeping.

A buried library book that is automatically added to the Museum collection and can then be read there.

Ginger Island's exploration currency, given to parrots to unlock routes, buildings, and services.

A stronger, rarer wood resource obtained mainly from large stumps, large logs, and mahogany trees.
Stored animal feed obtained from grass or purchased from Marnie and kept in a Silo or chest.

An oversized crop formation created when certain mature crops occupy a valid grid and transform overnight.

A reward token inserted into the Prize Machine in Mayor Lewis's house to receive the next prize in its sequence.
